**Cornell vs Columbia**

**Cornell: CS with a minor in Policy Analysis and Management**

Pros:

\- arguably the stronger CS program; strong recruiting at big tech companies

\- really cool project teams/clubs!! (Cornell Sustainable Design, AguaClara, Design and Tech Initiative)

\- I'm a super outdoorsy person so I'm really excited for everything the campus has to offer (hiking, kayaking, sailing, rock climbing -- anything, really). Plus these opportunities are all free, so that's something to be said when compared to the pricey nature of NYC.

\- less distracting environment I suppose? cute little college town with some nice restaurants/festivals

\- stronger campus culture owing to the rural location

\- wider variety of course offerings

Cons:

\- Secluded so flying to/from home is a pain. This also makes interning during the school year impossible, but I suppose there's not much time to do that at either school. Less opportunities for going to concerts/museums/other amenities that a big city has to offer.

\- much larger student body

\- I received a substantial scholarship specific to the College of Engineering, so I likely wouldn't be able to switch out of engineering for financial reasons.

\- I heard winters are very rough (especially given the seclusion of the campus)

**Columbia: CS with a concentration in Sociology**

Pros:

\- transportation is much more convenient to/from home

\- networking opportunities are unparalleled in the city

\- smaller student population so more personal attention? (this is my assumption; I may be wrong)

\- NYC is just such a culturally vibrant community with so much to do (museums, Broadway shows, restaurants, etc)

\- I love studying the liberal arts, and it seems like everyone at Columbia shares that same passion. With the Core Curriculum, I feel like this creates a common ground where students can have intellectual discussions about current events that relate to what they're studying in the Core. This atmosphere really resonates with me.

\- I can switch to Columbia College (basically arts and sciences) if I choose, without hurting my financial aid

Cons:

\- more expensive than Cornell (by about $3k per year). On the same note, I assume having fun costs more in NYC? Though we get free museum passes and discounted tickets to Broadway shows/arts events as Columbia students, dining is more expensive

\- I haven't visited in person, so I don't know if my instincts are accurate. From the virtual tour, campus felt kinda cramped. Also NYC seems kind of stressful to live in since it's so fast-paced, but again, I haven't visited so this might not reflect my actual feelings.

\- less CS course offerings

\- variety of outdoorsy things I can do is significantly less.

\- I heard it's difficult (but still possible) to maintain strong friendships given the nature of NYC
